title: Find the fake coin in two weighings
statement: You have nine identical-looking coins. One is heavier than the rest. You get a balance scale and two weighings. Find the heavy coin — guaranteed, not just usually.
solutionSteps: Split the nine coins into three groups of three: $A$, $B$, $C$.
Weighing 1: put $A$ against $B$. If one side sinks, the heavy coin is in that group. If they balance, it is in $C$. Either way you now have just three suspects.
Weighing 2: take the suspect group and weigh any one of its coins against any other.
If one of those two sinks, that is your coin. If they balance, it is the third one you left off the scale.

Why three groups and not halves: each weighing has three possible outcomes (left, right, balanced), so two weighings distinguish $3^2 = 9$ cases — exactly the number of coins. Halving would only get you $2^2 = 4$.
